text.content:
Virtue Traits are the spiritual endurance with which a character fights against the pull of the Beast. Every vampire has three Virtues, and each ranges from 1 to 5 Traits.

Conscience/Conviction

Your degree of adherence to your chosen morality. A character following Humanity uses Conscience - high Traits here mean genuine remorse for wrongdoing, which keeps the Beast from eroding your morality further. A character on an alternate Path of Enlightenment instead uses Conviction, measuring unwavering devotion to that Path's inhuman code rather than guilt.

Self-Control/Instinct

The ability to guide or resist frenzy. High Traits here help fight off berserk rage or the pull of hunger. Followers of Humanity use Self-Control; characters on Paths that lean into the Beast rather than restrain it instead use Instinct, and a character with high Instinct doesn't so much resist frenzy as choose when to direct it.

Courage

Battles against Rötschreck, the Red Fear that grips a vampire confronted by fire or sunlight. With many Courage Traits, a character can withstand the terror those threats provoke long enough to act rationally instead of fleeing outright.

Morality Trait

A character's Morality Trait total is the average of their Conscience/Conviction and Self-Control/Instinct ratings, rounded up - a single number from 1 to 5 that shows how closely they hold to their chosen ethical code. It governs things like staying awake during the day, rising from torpor, and dealing with mortals, and it also determines what circumstances call for a Virtue Test.

Virtue Tests

When pressed by overwhelming stress, rage, or fear, a vampire may attempt a Virtue Test - a Static Challenge against a Storyteller-set difficulty - to resist succumbing to the Beast. A tie is not enough to resist; the Virtue rating must exceed the difficulty. No character is ever required to attempt a Virtue Test - relenting and automatically losing is always an option. Losing means a lapse of virtue (a debilitating Negative Trait or complication, per the Virtue involved); one retest is allowed by risking a Trait of the same Virtue, and losing that retest can add a temporary derangement on top of the normal loss.

See also: the Frenzy / Rötschreck tool on the character sheet resolves both Self-Control/Instinct and Courage Virtue Tests automatically.
